method.description: Attempted official download of the five Delaware expungement documents, characterisation of what refused the requests, and reconstruction of the five identities from a retained repository capture of the Delaware Courts' own forms index rather than from a live fetch. Identity was established without touching the blocked perimeter; only currentness depends on it.
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires preserving the 403/WAF disposition distinctly, recording attended-retrieval evidence only, and never relabelling the source as generically missing or inferring an alternative. The WAF is characterised to the product family and its behaviour. No source is relabelled missing. No alternative is inferred: the LegalEase replica page held in the corpus is expressly rejected rather than used, and Form 281E is expressly refused as a substitute for Form 281.

blockCharacterisation.headline: The Delaware perimeter does not return 403. It returns 200 OK with a 247-byte body reading 'Request Rejected'. Every status-code-based success check passes against a document that was never served.
blockCharacterisation.whyThisMattersMoreThanTheBlockItself: An acquisition pipeline that keys on HTTP status would record five successful downloads, hash 247 bytes of rejection HTML, and pin those digests as official provenance for a petition, an extension sheet and two court orders. The block is ordinary; the false success signal is the hazard.

evidence.bodyVerbatim:
The requested URL was rejected. Please consult with your administrator.

Your support ID is: 15117310737377602000

[Go Back]
evidence.noServerBanner: The response carries no Server header. The 'Request Rejected / support ID' body together with this header set is the signature of an F5 BIG-IP Application Security Manager policy.
evidence.supportIdSignificance: A different support ID on every request proves the WAF is evaluating each request live. This is not a cached error page, a stale CDN object or a broken route — it is an active policy decision taken per request.

scope.finding: The rejection is not specific to the forms endpoint and not specific to the Judiciary.

probes.note: a different State of Delaware agency behind the same policy
a distinct condition from the WAF rejection; this host does not answer at all

scope.conclusion: A State of Delaware perimeter policy covering at least the Judiciary and the Department of Justice, not a courts-specific or forms-specific rule.
scope.userAgentIrrelevant: The identical rejection is returned to a default automated client and to an ordinary browser user-agent string.

distinctFrom.notAMissingSource: All five documents are published by the Delaware Courts and are listed in the Judiciary's own forms index, a capture of which this repository retains. Nothing is missing.
distinctFrom.notAnHttp403: This must not be recorded as a 403. It is a 200. Recording it as a 403 would make the two Delaware and Minnesota blocks look identical when their failure signatures are opposite, and would leave the false-success hazard undocumented.
distinctFrom.notAnUnreachableHost: The host resolves, completes TLS and returns a well-formed response. Contrast courts.mt.gov, which accepts no connection, and delcourts.delaware.gov above, which also does not answer.
distinctFrom.notACloudflareChallenge: There is no cf-mitigated header, no cf-ray, no JavaScript interstitial and no 'Just a moment' page. This is a different product with different behaviour from the Minnesota block characterised in the sibling job of this shard.

blockCharacterisation.remedy: An attended retrieval from a real browser session, which is the only legitimate route. No amount of automated retry, header adjustment or agent substitution is appropriate, and none was attempted.
whatWasNotDone: No attempt to evade, tune around or defeat the WAF policy.
No user agent spoofed beyond an ordinary browser string, which changed nothing.
No mirror, aggregator, cache or third-party reproduction retrieved in place of the issuer.
No alternative document inferred for any of the five identities.
The retained LegalEase replica page was expressly NOT used as a source.

prerequisitesInOrder: 1. Retrieve the five documents through an attended browser session at courts.delaware.gov.
2. Read the printed revision from each face and compare it against the index revision dates recorded here.
3. Admit five new rows to the successor edition.
4. Correct the FORM-281E role, title and workflow key, which does not wait on any of the above.
6. Only then author receipts with destinations under official-pdf/DE/.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: Five Delaware identities move from null titles, null issuers and no evidence to fully named documents with issuing court, style, role and index revision date, established without touching the blocked perimeter. A high-severity edition defect is surfaced that would have bound a 2018 charge extension sheet to a primary_filing component in place of a petition revised in 2025. The block itself is characterised as a WAF that returns HTTP 200, which is a pipeline hazard well beyond Delaware.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Delaware official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. None of the five assigned documents is retained, no bytes exist, currentness is unestablished, licensing is unresolved and unverifiable, generation is not permitted, runtime is disabled and no field map is built. terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: all five documents, titles, issuing courts, roles and index revision dates are established. It is not source_missing, which the stop condition forbids and which would be false — the Delaware Judiciary publishes all five and its own index lists them. It is not an HTTP 403 block: it is a 200, and conflating the two would erase the finding that matters most. And it is not acquired: not one byte of any assigned document was served.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Delaware's acquisition block is recorded as what it actually is: an F5 BIG-IP ASM policy that rejects automated requests while returning HTTP 200 OK with a 247-byte body and a support ID that rotates per request. That signature is now on record, and with it the hazard that a status-code-based pipeline would have booked five successful downloads of a rejection page and pinned its digest as official provenance for a petition and two court orders. All five assigned identities gain a title, an issuing court, a style, a role and an index revision date, reconstructed from a retained capture of the Judiciary's own index without touching the perimeter. A high-severity edition defect is surfaced: Form 281E, a 2018 charge extension sheet, is retained under a PETITION role with a title spliced from Form 281, while Form 281 itself — the Family Court petition revised 11/26/2025 — is unmanifested; that role and title correction can be made now and does not wait on the block. No binary is acquired, no receipt is created, nothing enters version control, no alternative is inferred, no replica is substituted, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
